:Judgment:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 18.11.2019 at about 12.15 p.m., the Petitioner was crossing road near bus stop, Byadarahalli, Magadi Main road, Bangalore, at that time, the driver of tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-2499 driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner came from Magadi main road and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was admitted to nearby Anupama hospital, Bangalore wherein he was given first aid treatment and thereafter shifted to Fortis hospital,
wherein he was taken treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical treatment, conveyance and the incidental expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as carpenter and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.
4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of tipper lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. Despite of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 has remained absent, hence placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through its counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending tipper lorry.
Further it contended that the accident was caused solely due to negligence of the petitioner only as he was crossing main road without taking any precautions where no zebra crossing lines.
Further it admits the issuance of insurance in respect of the tipper lorry.

Further it contended that the driver of the insured vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle and the owner of the tipper lorry entrusted the vehicle to a person who was not having valid driving licence.
Further it contended that the insured vehicle has no permit to ply in a public place.

Further it contended that owner of the insured tipper lorry has not intimated the alleged accident to this respondent and there is violation of Section 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Gurusiddachar Alias Gurumurthy vs Ravi Kumar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14107071/
2 Vehicles Act.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he sustained grievous injuries in the nature of permanent disablement on 18.11.2019 at about 12.15 p.m. near Bydarahalli bus stop, Bengaluru Magadi main road, Bydarahalli, Bengaluri, in an accident arising due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-2499?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation? If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award?
7.
In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.9.
Thereafter, the petitioner got examined 3 witnesses as PW.2 to P.W.4 and got marked document as per Ex.P.10 to 24 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondents have not adduced any evidence.

8. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for Petitioner and the learned Counsel for Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 9. Issue No.1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 18.11.2019 at about 12.15 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the tipper lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-2499 by its driver.
10. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-41-C-2499 by its driver.
11. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P-9.
He has re-iterated the Petition averments in his chief-affidavit.

Ex.P-1 to 9 are the true copies of FIR, Complaint, charge sheet, Spot mahazar, Seizure mahaar, IMV report, Wound certificate, discharge summaries, Ex.P.8 is the Medical bills and Ex.P.9 is the Gurusiddachar Alias Gurumurthy vs Ravi Kumar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14107071/

Upon going through Ex.P.1 and 2 FIR and Complaint, they justify the fact that on the complaint lodged before Byadarahalli Police Station, the concerned Police have registered the case against the driver of tipper lorry bearing Regn.No.KA-41-C-2499 for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 337 of IPC.

The Ex.P.3 Charge sheet shows that after thorough investigation, the Byadaarahalli Police have Charge- sheeted the driver of the offending tipper lorry for the offences punishable under Sec.279, 338 of IPC and 134(A&B) r/w Sec.187 of MV Act.
Ex.P.4 is the copy of spot mahazar which shows that it was made in the presence of panchas at the accident spot.
It further show that the road is measuring 40 feet width and the accident took place at 8 feet away from the footpath.
Ex.P.5 is the vehicle seizure mahazar, it shows that the offending lorry has been seized.
The Ex.P.6 is the Wound certificate which shows that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.7 are the discharge summaries which show that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient for the injuries sustained in the RTA.
Ex.P.8 is the medical bills and Ex.P.9 is the notarised copy of aadhar card.

13. Further, Petitioner has examined Medical record Officer as PW.2 and got marked Exs.P.10 to 14 i.e., authorization letter, entire case sheet, true copy of police intimation, copy of MLC extract and X-ray.
Petitioner has examined senior consultant neurosurgeon as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 19 i.e., OPD record, Neuro physiological assessment report, MMSE report, Audiogram report and X-ray.

Further got examined another Medical record Officer as PW.4 and got marked Ex.P.20 to 24 i.e., Authorization letter, copy of MLC register extract, MLC intimation letter, prescription and CT scan report.
14. To rebut the evidence of P.W.1, the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 cross examined the P.W.1.
In the cross- examination P.W.1 has admitted that while he was crossing the road, the accident took place.
He has admitted that the place of the accident is the Magadi-Bengaluru main road and wherein many vehicles do ply.
There is no divider in the middle of the road and there are footpath on both sides of the road.
There is no zebra crossing and sky walker at the said place.

15. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 argued that the accident was happened when the petitioner was crossing the road where there is no zebra-crossing, hence contributory negligence to be considered.
16. In the case on hand, it is the case of the petitioner that while he was crossing the road the accident has occurred.
But he has not stated whether he was crossing the road on Zebra lines which meant for pedestrian crossing.
But in the cross examination, the PW.1 specifically admitted that there was no Zebra lines at the place of accident.
It is relevant to state here that the recitals of the spot Panchnama made clear that the accident was took place at 8 feet away from the footpath.
Hence, it is clear that the petitioner was already crossed 8 feet from footpath and he was almost at middle of the road.
Of course the driver of the vehicles ought to have been more prudent while driving.

But, it cannot be lost sight of the fact that a duty is also cast on a pedestrian and he should use due care and caution in going upon and crossing the road and it is his duty to look out for oncoming traffic.

Whenever a pedestrian is crossing over a roadway at any place other than which is meant for pedestrian crossing, they cannot claim any specific precedence and the responsibility for Gurusiddachar Alias Gurumurthy vs Ravi Kumar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14107071/

sentences.text: causing the accident more often than not will have to be shared by the pedestrian along with the vehicle driver.
In view of this, it cannot be said that it was only the driver of the vehicle in question was solely responsible for the accident.
In view of the fact that the claimant had crossed the road where he was not supposed to cross certain degree of contributory negligence will have to be attributed to him.

Therefore, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has admitted that there is no zebra crossing and sky walking at the said place.
Therefore, the accident is occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and the petitioner.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the driver of the tipper lorry attributed 90% of negligence towards the said accident and the petitioner has attributed 10% of the negligence towards the said accident.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 "Partly in the Affirmative".

17. Issue No. 2 : As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending tipper lorry by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
18. In the petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 53 years.
He has produced Aadhar card marked at ExP.9 to prove his age.
As per aadhar card, his date of birth is shown as 1969.
The accident has taken place on 18.11.2019.
Hence, the age of the Petitioner as on the date of accident is taken as 50 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
19. Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as carpenter and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to prove avocation and income.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e., Rs.14,000/-p.m. as the accident has been occurred in the year of 2019, for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
20. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
21.
It is to be noted here that according to the petitioner, he has sustained grievous injuries.
Ex.P.6 wound certificate shows that the Petitioner had sustained following injuries.
1. Head injury with right sub dural hemorrhage.
2. Fracture of left temporal and parietal bone.
Further, the Doctor has opined that the said injuries grievous are in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that, awarding compensation of Rs.40,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
22. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
23.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 18.11.2019 to 22.11.2019 and from 22.11.2019 to 27.11.2019 at Fortis Hospital.
Further, P.W.3 Dr.Shailesh A V Rao has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
The discharge summaries marked at Ex.P.7 also justify the same Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient for 9 days.
24. For this he might have taken atleast two months for recovery.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.28,000/- under this head (@ Rs.14,000/- per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
25.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period,
the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.6,000/- towards attendants charges, Rs.6,000/- towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.6,000/- towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.18,000/- under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENSES :
26. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent more than Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 9 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.8 which is totally amounting to Rs.12,766/-.
In the cross-examination of PW.1 learned counsel for Respondent No.2 suggested that the bills do not have seal and signature.
But PW.1 denies the same and shows ignorance to the question that Ex.P.8 Sl.8 is the advance receipt.
I have gone through the medical bills.
Sl.1, 2 and 7 had signature and Sl.No.5 and 6 do have seal and signature
Hence these bill are acceptable bills.
Sl. No.3
and 4 do not have seal and signature and Sl.No.6 to 8 are deposit receipt.
Hence these bills and receipts have to be deducted.
Hence acceptable bills are Sl.No.1, 2, and 5 amounting Rs.4943.

Hence, by rounding Gurusiddachar Alias Gurumurthy vs Ravi Kumar on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/14107071/

VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

27. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and he is still unable to do carpentry work efficiently as he was doing prior to the accident.
28.

Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Shailesh.A.V.Rao who is senior consultant neurosurgeon as PW.3 and got marked Exs.P.15 to 19 i.e., OPD record, Neuro physiological assessment report, MMSE report, Audiogram report and X-ray.
He assessed whole body disability at 33%.
29. In the cross-examination, PW.3 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
One Dr.Jayanthi has given neuro physiological assessment report.
The score of GCS was 15/15 at the time of assessment.
The said score is normal as per the guidelines.
Now, eye opening score is normal, but, at the time of accident it was E-3.
He has admitted that moto response is normal and the line of treatment was conservative management.
While assessing the disability the patient was answering most of the questions.
He further admitted that he has seen the audiogram report for assessment of disability in respect of hearing.
The disability which he has assessed includes loss of hearing.
Audiogram report was submitted by Audiologist.
He has admitted that the disabilities he has shown in his affidavit are only in respect of neuro related issues and it does not include Ortho related issues.
30. The Doctor has assessed disability of the petitioner to the whole body of 33%.

As discussed above the deposition of PW.3 -Doctor coupled with the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.6 and the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.7 would show that the petitioner had sustained head injury with right sub dural hemorrhage with minimal midline shaft, fracture left temporal and parietal bone and accelerated hypertension.

Upon careful consideration of the assessment of disability made by PW.3, keeping in mind the fact that PW.1 personally appeared before this court and deposed, also keeping in mind the nature of injuries sustained by PW.1 and the treatment which he has taken, it can safely be said that there is functional disability of 25%.

The petitioner had sustained right SDH and fracture left temporal and parietal bone and accelerated hypertension, as such the physical disability stated by PW.3 at 33% can be held to translate into the functional disability of 25%.

sentences.text: As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of Rs.14,000/- per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 25%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.4,62,000/- (Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 11 x 25/100 =Rs.4,62,000/-).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,62,000/-under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 40,000/-
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/-
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 18,000/-
diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 5,000/-
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 28,000/-
laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs.4,62,000/-

Total Rs.5,83,000/-
Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,83,000/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending tipper lorry bearing Reg. No.KA-41-C-2499 and also petitioner.
34. There is no dispute of the fact that the respondent No.1 is the owner and the respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending tipper lorry in question.
There is no dispute of the fact that the policy in respect of said vehicle was valid and effective as on the date of accident.
Hence, respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay 90% compensation amount i.e., Rs.5,24,700/- to the petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
35. ISSUE No.3
